content.user_title: Audit Statistical Reporting for Nature Journals
content.value_statement: Manuscripts often omit design details or overstate statistical evidence. This skill audits reporting and drafts precise revisions without inventing missing facts.
actual_capabilities: Audits statistical methods and results for missing reporting details.
Distinguishes independent units, biological replicates, technical replicates, and repeated measurements.
Checks p values, effect sizes, uncertainty intervals, assumptions, and multiple-comparison reporting.
Reviews figure legends for sample sizes, error bars, tests, and annotations.
Drafts conservative manuscript revisions and responses to statistical reviewer comments.
Applies Nature and Nature Machine Intelligence reporting checklists when relevant.
limitations: Cannot infer experimental design facts that the user does not provide.
Does not replace expert statistical consultation or validate every analysis.
Raw-data reanalysis requires data, metadata, and an explicit computation request.
Shared Nature Machine Intelligence guidance may be unavailable outside the original repository layout.

use_cases.title: Prepare a journal submission
use_cases.description: Audit Methods, Results, and legends, then produce conservative revisions and a list of missing author facts.

use_cases.title: Assess statistical reporting
use_cases.description: Identify unsupported claims, unclear replication, incomplete tests, and reporting gaps before editorial decisions.

use_cases.title: Standardize manuscript support
use_cases.description: Apply a repeatable checklist across research groups and draft focused questions for authors.

prompt_templates.title: Review a methods section
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this Statistical analysis section for missing details. Mark uncertain facts as AUTHOR_INPUT_NEEDED and provide a revised version: [paste text]
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of one manuscript section

prompt_templates.title: Check a figure legend
prompt_templates.prompt: Check this figure legend for independent n, replication, error bars, tests, corrections, and exact p-value reporting: [paste legend]

prompt_templates.title: Answer a reviewer
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this reviewer comment and manuscript excerpt. List required statistical changes, draft revised wording, and prepare a conservative response: [paste materials]

prompt_templates.title: Run a consistency audit
prompt_templates.prompt: Cross-check these Methods, Results, legends, and tables for statistical consistency. Map each claim to evidence and rank unresolved issues: [paste sections]

output_examples.input: Audit a methods paragraph that reports t-tests and n values without defining the experimental unit.
output_examples.output: Major issue: the experimental unit is undefined, so n may represent technical observations. Provide the unit and replicate hierarchy before selecting a final test.

output_examples.input: Rewrite a figure legend with error bars, star notation, and no correction method.
output_examples.output: Revised legend: Data show mean and 95% confidence interval. n denotes independent animals. Exact p values use the stated corrected comparison.

best_practices: Provide the Methods, Results, legends, and relevant reviewer comments together when possible.
State the experimental unit, replicate structure, group sizes, exclusions, and correction strategy.
Confirm every proposed revision against actual analyses before manuscript submission.
anti_patterns: Do not ask the skill to invent missing sample sizes, tests, or p values.
Do not treat cells, images, or technical repeats as independent units without design evidence.
Do not use wording improvements as proof that the underlying analysis is valid.

faq.question: Does this skill perform statistical reanalysis?
faq.answer: It supports bounded reanalysis only when you provide suitable data, metadata, and an explicit request.

faq.question: Can it review Chinese manuscript notes?
faq.answer: Yes. It can interpret Chinese or English notes and produce publication-ready statistical wording.

faq.question: Is it limited to Nature?
faq.answer: No. It targets Nature reporting but can apply conservative principles to other high-impact journals.

faq.question: Will it fill missing statistical details?
faq.answer: No. It marks missing facts as AUTHOR_INPUT_NEEDED instead of inventing values, tests, or procedures.

faq.question: Can it infer replication from a figure?
faq.answer: It can flag reporting gaps, but experimental units and independence require author confirmation.

faq.question: What information should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide study design, experimental units, sample sizes, replicate structure, tests, corrections, figures, and relevant text.
